content.text:
I'd go with the second one. Pretty sure. The thing that decided it: under the S&P 500 it says "חמש מאות החברות הגדולות בארצות הברית". That's the first time anyone has told me in plain words what the S&P everyone at work talks about actually is. The first option only gives the index name, so if I didn't already know "ת"א-125" or "MSCI AC World" I'd get nothing from it.

**How it went:**
- **Where I looked:** Both screens show the same list of four funds, so they're two versions, not one long page. On each I read the heading "קרנות סל 4 קרנות", then the fund names, then the green index names ("ת"א-125", "ת"א-90", "S&P 500", "MSCI AC World"). Then the fees on the left. I went straight to the S&P row: "0.8% קבוע", "0.3% משתנה", "0.015% נאמן". Then the second screen, where the only thing I noticed was the new text under the index names. I read the S&P and the 125 ones ("מאה עשרים וחמש החברות בעלות השווי הגבוה ביותר בבורסה בתל אביב").
- **What I skipped:** The grey line under the heading. The fund numbers (1148808 and so on). The "בדף הקרן במאיה" links. The small grey labels on the right after the first one or two.
- **Where I got stuck:** Each fund has three fees. I don't know if I'm meant to add them up or which one I'd actually pay. 0.8% sounds like nothing, but on the S&P it's the highest one on the list, and I didn't know if that's a lot. There are no shekels anywhere, so I couldn't tell what it would cost on my 30,000.
- **Words I didn't get:** "נאמן", "צוברת", "עסקת החלף", "(4A)" / "(4D)", "משתנה" next to "קבוע".
- **What bothered me:** "מס גם על שינויי המטבע" scared me off the S&P a bit. It sounds like a tax I'd pay on top. Also, "חשיפה לדולר" is on the right side in the first option and I nearly missed it there. In the second the labels wrap onto two lines, which is a bit messy but OK.
- **Would I have left?** No, it's short. But I didn't come away knowing what to do first, and nothing says which fund is the "normal" one to pick.
